prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts a repair workshop floor sloping away from the downward-looking camera wearer as they turn right and approach a group of people and scooters across the 5 frames. In frame 1, a workbench surface and a vertical tire on the right are within arm's reach at 0.5–1.2 m, while in frames 2–3 a dismantled white scooter on the lower right (1–1.5 m) and a green bin on the left (1.5–2 m) sit below and in front of two standing people and a second white scooter roughly 2–3 m away, spaced 0.5–1 m apart from each other. Across frames 4–5, the camera wearer moves within 0.4–1 m of the person seated on the left scooter—whose crossed arms and torso become bright white and within arm's reach on the left while the standing person at 0.8–1.2 m is pushed to the far-left edge and occluded in frame 5—and the dismantled scooter and loose tires remain below on the right floor at 1.2–2 m. The depth map makes the continuous 3D floor gradient, the vertical relief of the loose tires on the ground, and the exact depth ordering between the overlapping people and scooter parts much clearer than the cluttered, motion-blurred RGB frames. However, the map is unreliable inside the hollow center of the frame 1 tire where the background is filled in too brightly, along over-smoothed tool and wheel edges on the floor, and in the upper corners where mid-ground walls and ramps drop abruptly to black.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates key foreground actors and vehicles in the workshop as the camera wearer turns from the workbench in frame 1 toward two people beside a white scooter in frames 2–5. In frame 1 it labels the upright tire at 1 m as a motorcycle, and in frames 2–3 it segments the lower-right dismantled scooter (1–1.5 m, merged with a nearby ramp) as a motorcycle while separating the standing person on the left (2–2.5 m, bodies cropped at the top edge) from the person straddling the upper-left white scooter about 0.5–1 m to their right. In frames 4–5, as the camera wearer approaches to within 0.5–1 m of the person straddling the scooter (who faces forward-right with arms crossed and head angled down, not looking at the camera wearer), the masks show the left standing person (facing right) shifting to the far-left edge in frame 4 before disappearing out of view in frame 5, while the seated person fills the left foreground within arm's reach. Compared to the RGB strip, the colour-coded masks clearly distinguish the overlapping silhouettes of the two dark-clothed people from the dark scooter seat and cluttered workshop background in frames 2–4. However, the map is unreliable where it misclassifies a single tire as a motorcycle in frame 1, splits one person into two person masks in frames 3 and 4, merges the person and scooter into overlapping motorcycle/person masks in frame 5, mislabels the upper-right red lift ramp at 2.5 m as a parking meter in frame 5, and completely misses the white scooter under the rider in frames 2–4, the green bin, floor tires, and the camera wearer's blue-gloved right hand at the bottom of frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map is completely blank (all black) across all 5 frames, failing to render any yellow body keypoints or magenta hand skeletons despite the presence of two people and the camera wearer's hand in the RGB strip. In the RGB context, two people stand 0.5–1 m apart in the upper-left mid-ground at 2–3 m in frames 2–3 (with heads cropped above the top frame boundary), and come within 0.4–1.2 m on the left in frames 4–5 as the camera wearer steps into arm's reach of them. From the RGB frames alone, the person on the white scooter faces forward-right with crossed arms and looks downward away from the camera wearer while the second person stands to their left facing right with one hand near their hip in frame 4, and the camera wearer's own blue-gloved right hand enters the lower-center foreground at 0.3 m in frame 5 within reach of a metal part and the seated person's hip. Because no skeletons are detected, this map provides no spatial information beyond what is visible in the RGB image and cannot resolve the exact joint angles of the crossed arms or the occluded lower legs behind the scooter and frame edges. The pose estimator is completely unreliable here due to the high downward egocentric viewing angle, severe upper-body and head cropping at the frame boundaries, motion blur in frame 1, and self-occlusion from heavy dark jackets and crossed arms.
